notes.title: Steam Deck update and bit more on the fate of Fera
notes.content:
Hey Fera faithfuls, thanks for your patience and your continued support!! After our much needed holiday break, I'm pleased to announce that our latest patch includes the much awaited Steam Deck compatibility! (please read the update notes down below)

In our original "State of Fera and our Studio" update, we discussed our "Hail Mary" plan for Fera. As of Jan 3, our base price for Fera has been switched to $9 USD. But we are not exiting out of Early Access and calling it a 1.0, we feel the state of our game isn't near what we would consider a 1.0 release yet and to do so would be disingenuous. 

However, we feel $9 USD is a fair price for the 30+ hrs of gameplay that our game currently provides, some jankiness not wishstanding. Our team is quite thrilled to see a rise in positive reviews for our game since we lowered the price point. Please write a review if you enjoyed the game, it really helps us and our dream is to get out of the MIXED rating.

As for further development of Fera, we are solely dependent on the incoming Steam revenue to fund it. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44536685/9b6bb72cd1377f75b08ad36dac77bab99d2a66de.png[/img] 

What the image shows is the full Lifetime Steam Revenue for Fera to date.  [b]Our share of that was $36K[/b], we used up most of it for the patches leading up to the this latest one. We'll let the revenue collect up a bit while we finish up some milestones for our next project (which is the crucial thing with funding that allows to continue as a studio) but we hope to be able to get some more development resources on it if revenues build up enough by March/April.  

In the meantime, please enjoy the latest update, we will keep you posted if any big JUMPS in revenue will allow us to pursue development sooner.

Thanks again for your continued support and warm wishes, we feel like we have the best of the Steam community with us on this journey.

With love, 
The Massive Damage Team

[h1]0.7.1.0 - Steam Deck Compatibility is Here![/h1]
We’ve been hard at work optimizing Fera to lower the minimum specs and make it playable on Steam Deck! Steam Deck support has been the number one thing we've been asked about throughout development, so we're excited to make it official!
That being said, to get consistent 30 FPS on the Steam Deck, you’ll need to adjust some settings. Here’s what we recommend:
Upscaling Method: AMD FSR 3
Quality Mode: Ultra Performance
Quality Level: Medium
Also, you'll want to make sure your Steam Deck has the latest OS update.
As part of this effort, we’ve enhanced the visuals for Medium settings while also sneaking in some improvements to the High settings, in addition to other optimizations. For those details, check out the notes below.
Thank you for your continued support, and happy holidays from the Fera team!
[b]STEAM DECK COMPATIBILITY
[/b]1.1 Fera is now fully playable on Steam Deck! This update includes key optimizations (see below) as well as adjustments to non-gameplay features, such as the addition of virtual keyboard support and layout changes designed to suit Steam Deck’s hardware.
[b]OPTIMIZATIONS[/b]
2.1 Foliage scalability settings have been enhanced to provide deeper performance savings, particularly on low and medium settings.
2.2 Selective optimizations have been applied to Lumen and Nanite, reducing their performance impact while maintaining high visual fidelity.
2.3 Better use of distance-based World Position Offset (WPO) phasing has been implemented across world assets, improving performance in larger environments while preserving detail. (edited)

notes.title: MAJOR UPDATE 0.7.0.0 (Early Access Founders Pack and Tons of Improvements)
notes.content:
[h1]0.7.0.0  Founder's Pack And Improvements[/h1]
We recognize that this drastic price decrease by 70% will be unfair to those who bought our game early. As mentioned before this price decrease is the only shot we have left at possibly keeping this game alive so we can keep working on it.
For those early purchasers at the original price,we've come up with an Early Access Founders Pack that will be unlocked for you.
The Early Access Founders Pack includes:
    1) a new metallic glider, accessible in the options menu
    2) gorgeous purple VFX flying trails (also accessible in the options menu)
    3) a Baby Thunderhorn that you can add to your village (you just need to build a pen for them)
Thanks again for your early support of Fera!
[b]EARLY ACCESS FOUNDERS PACK	
[/b]
1.1   3 new cosmetic items for players who have bought the game before the price reduction. These include a new glider, new glide vfx and a baby Thunderhorn.
[b]GAMEPLAY TWEAKS
[/b]
2.1 We've loostened the rules around dodge roll and collision so that a portion of the dodge roll can now phase through monsters. This allows you to much more easily dislodge yourself from under a monster, and allows you to get out from under a monster corpse.
2.2 Scaleback hitboxes were triggering a tad early, resulting in unfair hits on players.
2.3 The initial portion of the dodge roll has been sped up 60%, which ups its usefulness.
[b]NEW STATION: INVENTOR'S DESK	
[/b]
3.1 A new station now becomes available at Tribe Lvl 3 that allows for the creation of healing potions, bouncy jumpshrooms (that send you flying up into the air) and deployable grapple jellyfish, each of which you can bring with you into the underland.
[b]PROGRESSION CHANGES
[/b]
4.1 From the outset, we're now giving players two tether charges, air boost and all the heavy jump attacks for each weapon. For this purpose, we're giving all existing players a free skill refund, that will allow you to refund all your skills down to the starting state, which will gift you the skill points you initially spent on those skills.
4.2 Players starting stamina has been doubled.
[b]FIXES[/b]
5.1 There was a bug that could dissapear all bindsaps from the world upon reloading.
5.2 In single player, going to the options screen could unpause the game. That's now fixed.
5.3 There was an issue where changing languages wasn't working as expected. That's now fixed.
5.4 There was an issue where the player was sometimes told to open a portal to allow a villager to work on a task in the village, when they shouldn't have to. That should now be fixed."
[b]UI[/b]
6.1 You can now see your resource category maximums at all times, allowing you to make better decisions about what tasks to select and what resources to pursue.
[b]ADDITIONS[/b]
7.1 There's a new REPORT ISSUES bug right on the title screen and options screen. Please use it to report any issue that you find. Thanks!
[b]VILLAGE BEHAVIOUR CHANGES
[/b]
8.1 Villagers now move 33% faster, so should be performing a brisk jog at most times.
8.2 Villagers no longer need to walk to the stockpile to get their resources for performing a task.
8.3 Villagers can now work at 50% speed even when at 0 stamina.  They will still receive a happiness penalty if they end the day with zero stamina, though, so watch out.
8.4 Players can add task completion points to tasks even when a villager isn't doing a task.
[b]AUDIO CHANGES
[/b]
9.1 The combat music volume has been tuned down considerably.

Thank you all again for your early support!
- Massive Damage Team

notes.title: The Fate of Fera (and our studio)
notes.content:
First we want to thank our early supporters and community for Fera. We learned a lot from your valuable feedback (both good and bad) and we’re sorry we were not able to deliver a better Early Access experience.

We made a lot of mistakes with our development and launch of Fera: The Sundered Tribes. As our first 3D Open World multiplayer game, we definitely bit off more than we could chew and there’s no blame to be laid on anyone or anything except for ourselves.

[h3]Honest numbers for Fera[/h3]
Here’s the honest math regarding the sales of Fera:
- Lifetime Net Revenue: $110k
- Massive Damage take home 20% (our investors are owed the rest): $22K
- This is all we’re expected to see from the first 2 months of sales.
- Due to the lackluster sales, we could not afford to keep our team of 26 people so unfortunately we had to lay off 60% of the studio.
- We’re doing our best to help them find contract work and other opportunities.
- Because our studio is entirely reliant on publisher funding, the majority of our team has to work on a new unannounced project (for which we have already secured funding)
- Despite the flaws we are still proud of what we tried to accomplish with Fera and we would love to find a way to keep working on it if possible.

[h3]Hail Mary plan for saving Fera[/h3]
We’ve come up with a Hail Mary plan that might be able to allow us to generate enough revenue to be able to hire (or hire back) resources to keep improving and adding to Fera if it succeeds. Here’s our plan:

- As of Nov 27, Fera will be on sale for 70% off until Jan 3rd.
- We feel this price drop is necessary to make Fera in its early state a much more attractive and fair price.
- We will attempt to fix some of the major issues with the game before this sale goes live.
- After the Autumn and Winter sales, Fera will release to v1.0 with a new BASE price of $9.99
- As the current game has about 25-35hrs of gameplay, we hope this will attract new players while still giving good value for the $9
- If we find a new life after the price drop and we are able to make enough revenue to hire people to work on the game we will do so (and let you all know our plans if so)]
- We’ve talked to a bunch of our fellow developers and some publishers about our plan and most agree it’s worth a shot.
- We’re being 100% transparent about this because we feel it’s the best approach and everyone who thinks about buying Fera for $9 will know what to expect and go in with open eyes.

Thanks again to everyone who believed in Fera and in us, we’ll do our best to keep the project alive as soon as it makes the revenue needed to hire on devs to continue the development.

For those early buyers we are working to make exclusive Founders Only glider wings and a pet for your village as a thank you for supporting us at launch.

Next steps:
- Quality of Life patch and exclusive Founders Only items update
- Autumn sale starts Nov 27 and the discount will be 70% off
- Custom sale at 70% bridging the gap between Autumn and Winter sale
- Winter sale at 70% off
- Fera v1.0 launch on Jan 3rd (our one and only shot at Steam visibility) at $9.99 with a 10% discount.

notes.title: Patch 4 (Major Optimizatiom Patch) is out!
notes.content:
[h1]0.6.7.0 - Major Optimization Patch[/h1]
Thank you all for your patience, we’ve heard your feedback regarding performance, and over the past two weeks, we’ve been focused on optimization.
The performance issues were most prominent in foliage-heavy areas, with the Northern Forest being the most affected. Here’s what we observed:

- High-end machines (e.g., Ryzen 9 7950X3D + RTX 4090), which we expected to run at 60 FPS in 4K on High Quality, were averaging around 52.5 FPS, occasionally dropping as low as 40 FPS.
- Mid-range machines (e.g., Ryzen 5 5500 + AMD RX 7600), which we expected to hit 30 FPS at 1080p on High Quality, were averaging 27.5 FPS, with lows reaching 22 FPS.
After our optimizations, we’ve significantly improved performance in foliage-heavy areas:
-High-end machines now average 68.5 FPS at 4K on High Quality, with drops rarely going below 62.5 FPS, and never for prolonged periods.
- Mid-range machines now average 41.5 FPS at 1080p on High Quality, with dips rarely falling below 37 FPS, and never for prolonged periods.
Of course, performance can vary based on specific hardware setups, but overall, you can expect improvements in the range of 10-15 FPS. In short:
- High-end machines can now comfortably hit 60 FPS at 4K on High Quality.
- Mid-range machines can confidently achieve 30 FPS at 1080p on High Quality.
Thank you all for your patience on this topic!
On other topics, there were also a few additions for gameplay and quality-of-life. They're in the notes!

[b]OPTIMIZATION[/b]	
1.1  We've reduced the over-use of hardware occlusion in certain particle effect systems, which was unnecessarily straining the CPU.
1.2  Shadow rendering for foliage has been tuned to lower GPU costs with minimal impact on the overall look, providing smoother performance, especially in foliage-heavy areas.
1.3  Reflection settings have been optimized to reduce overall costs, improving performance while retaining visual quality."

[b]GAMEPLAY ADDITIONS[/b]
2.1 Each weapon has been given a distinct light gliding attack!

[b]QUALITY OF LIFE[/b]
3.1  We've added pop-ups to specify why multiplayer sessions fail, so it's less of a mystery.
3.2 The options menu has been reorganized to be a little less messy."

[b]CHANGES[/b]
4.1  The VFX for villager smoke now stays visible for a lot longer as you approach its position.
4.2  There were areas in the crater where it was easy for the player to get stuck. Those should be greatly alleviated.
FIXES
5.1  There was a collision issue wherein players could fall through the tops of mushrooms. That's now fixed.
5.2  There was an issue where villagers would float into the sky after being hit by monsters. That should no longer happen.
5.3  In multiplayer, clients were not having knockback properly applied. That should now be fixed.
5.4  There was an issue where you weren't able to select Geruth in the villager placement screen when you had more than 6 villagers (depending on the game screen width). That's now fixed.
5.5  There was an issue where when you refunded a station while its tasks were queued, that you'd lose the ability to schedule those tasks in the future.
TWEAKS
6.1  Quick Weapon swapping UI has been given a face lift.

notes.title: ⚡️ Patch 3 (v 0.6.6.0) is released! ⚡️
notes.content:
Thank you all for your patience and support! Here's our 3rd patch and it focuses on a bunch of QoL fixes.

NEW
1.1  Key Rebinding - You can now rebind your keys for both keyboard and controller from within the Options menu.
1.2  Quick Weapon Swapping - After marking your favorite weapon for each type in the Character screen, you can quickly cycle through them with a single button.
1.3  New Tether Light Attack and Cling Attack animations for hammer, spear and cleaversaw weapon types.
CHANGES
2.1  The Monster Harvester now automatically queues up all available tasks upon building and destroys itself when all tasks are completed.
2.2  Task assisting is now a toggled input instead of a held input.
2.3  Stamina cost of signature attacks reduced to 0.
2.4  Changed the default key binding for signature attacks to Q for keyboard.
2.5  Aiming with Tether Light Attacks improved by turning your character toward the target.
2.6  Likelihood of Tether Light Attack executions being interrupted by Clinging reduced.
2.7  Due to Tether Light Attack improvements, stamina costs have been reintroduced for them.
2.8  Damage adjustments to Tether Light Attacks and Cling Attacks.
2.9  Razorwings have gained a new tether point, allowing for easier targeting from below.
FIXES
3.1  Fixed an issue where signature attacks sometimes failed to execute.
3.2  The Master Volume slider in the Options screen now correctly affects UI audio.

notes.title: ⚡️ Patch 1 (v 0.6.5.4) is released!⚡️
notes.content:
⚡️ Patch 1 (v 0.6.5.4) is released! ⚡️
Thank you so much for checking out our game, and know that we're working hard to improve it! The launch didn't go as smooth as we had hoped but we're going to try to squash as many issues as we can, as soon as we can - starting with this!

MAJOR FIXES 🦖
1.1 There were lots of instances where players had trouble joining their friends' existing game due worlds with high density of buildings failing to load. That should now be fixed.
1.2 Similar to 1.1, the same problem could occur due to a build up of tracked event history in the game save. That is now also fixed.
1.3 Pressing ESC during the feast scene no longer pauses the game, giving the impression of a freeze.
1.4 You can no longer accidentally lose your position in the skill tree and have trouble recentering yourself.

MINOR FIXES 🐥
2.1 The camera zoomed in awkwardly when you equipped a Scaleback Spear. That shouldn't happen anymore.
2.2 Multiplayer clients had an issue where collectables took about 0.5s to register as collected. This felt off, but should now be fixed.
2.3 The big monster footsteps sound effects have been tweaked down.
2.4 There were some improper monster names in the tasks and weapons, along with some formatting artifacts. Those should be fixed now.
2.5 Tremorhoof Elders would give Frostfang rewards in carving and harvesting. That should now be fixed.

CHANGES 🦋
3.1 From lots off player feedback, we've realized we made stamina cost far too punishing in the early game, so we have revamped our stamina costs.
3.2 You can now perform light ground attack combos with no stamina cost whatsoever, allowing you greater ability to dodge and perform more heavy duty attacks when the opportunity arises. It should feel a lot more dynamic now.
- Reduced Cling Heavy attack stamina costs by 50%
- Cling Light attacks cost 0 stamina now
3.2 Players needed an option to heal themselves in the Underland, so we've opted to greatly improve the amount of health slain Jellions provide you (100 instead of 15). Now you should be excited to see them out in the wild (especially when you're in a combat with a huge monster).
3.3 Jellions have had their movement speed reduced down by 50%, as it was causing frustration.
3.4 There was much frustration with the starting storage limits in the early game, so those have been increased to 250 (New Worlds only). Each additional storage unit also increases capacity by 250.
3.5 Featherhides and Jellions health increased by 30% to counter the increased attack abilities by the player, allowed with the reduced stamina costs.

TWEAKS
4.1 We've added some SFX to the collectables when you collect them.
4.2 We've added some more robust looking grass visuals.

notes.title: Demo Feedback and The Road to Early Access
notes.content:
Thank you everyone who tried out our Alpha Demo of Fera: The Sundered Tribes for the Steam Next Fest and thank you for all the incredible feedback. Good or bad, we've taken your feedback and we're taking the time to collate, review, and discuss with our team.

The demo was a early build so we've taken it down since it will be not representative of the final game by the time we launch in Early Access (release date announcement trailer is coming soon).

Here's some of our major priorities that we will be focused on our road to launch:

[h3]Combat[/h3]
We're taking your feedback to heart and working to improve all aspects of combat. We have a task force assigned to work on this. Better hit mechanics and improved damage models and physics, we have big plans for combat. 

[h3]Hunting[/h3]
To support our brave hunters, we are building a monsterpedia to track the various beasts and behemoths you encounter. Researching the carcasses will reap rewards as you learn the various strengths and weaknesses of these monsters.

We're also working hard on making many new behemoths and monsters (and variants) for the launch.

[h3]Player Progression[/h3]
We're revamping the player character progression to have more granularity in your various stats and we will also be introducing a skill tree to unlock advanced combat and traversal moves.

[h3]UI[/h3]
We're doing a full UI revamp to make it much more intuitive and easier to use. 

[h3]Tutorial[/h3]
We're going to make a new tutorial that will be a tighter, more exciting experience to properly introduce the player to the world of Fera.

[h3]Multiplayer[/h3]
Last and definitely NOT least, is multiplayer. We're aiming to have 4 player co-op ready for the Early Access launch!

[h3]Join Us[/h3]
Thank you again for all the great feedback, we're going to be a bit heads down for the next few months working on all of the above. 

There is a Closed Beta for Fera: The Sundered Tribes that we will be announcing as we get closer to launch.

To apply for the Beta or join our growing Discord commmunity, hit us up here: [url=https://discord.com/invite/massivedamageinc]https://discord.com/invite/massivedamageinc[/url]

- Massive Damage  Team
